`python3 budget.py 2026-09` now counts only September's transactions, and running it with no argument gives the same all-time totals as before. I ran both against your data:

| Envelope | No month (all) | `2026-09` | `2026-08` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 371.55 | 403.05 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 124.75 | 78.10 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 84.25 | 111.50 |
| household | 54.61 | 101.60 | 73.01 |

- **Month with no transactions:** it shows every envelope at its full allocation rather than an error (e.g. `2026-07`).
- **Bad input:** a malformed month such as `2026-9`, or more than one argument, prints a message to stderr and exits with status 2.

The change is all in `budget.py`: two small helpers (`parse_month`, `in_month`) plus the argument handling in `main`, and the usage docstring is updated.
